doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Television, vocal albums and orchestral craft
title: Irving Townsend's concept and Jo Stafford's choices
summary: Mandel credits Columbia A&R man Irving Townsend with the concept for Jo + Jazz and says Jo chose the tunes, later reissued by Jo and Paul Weston.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Now for that album, was that your concept to use say, Ellington players with Jo?
Well, it wasn't really my concept, it was Irving Townsend's concept, at the time, you know he was the A and R man there and god bless Irving, you know we…
This was for Columbia in the late 50s and…
That CD by the way, you can get that record, its out on CD now.
I think Jo and Paul Weston put it out themselves right?
They did, on Corinth [Corinthian Records] I think, they bought the masters and put it out, I guess they liked that record.
Yeah, great people, both of them.
So Irving came up with the concept then?
He came up with the concept but Irving was wonderful at concepts, he was one of the great A and R men who have been forgotten. Not by me though.
Whose choice of tunes was it primarily Jo’s or did you have some suggestions for tunes or did Irving?
I think it was mostly let Jo chose them, anybody with the kind of taste she has, shouldn't be told what to do.
